content.text:
I've set up a new Rust project called `wintool` in `/work`, using Microsoft's official `windows` crate (v0.62) for the Windows API bindings. It type-checks and passes clippy and `cargo fmt` against the 64-bit Windows target. I haven't linked or run it: this machine is Linux and has no Windows linker, so the first real build and run needs to happen on Windows.

**Files:**
- **`Cargo.toml`**: The `windows` dependency only applies when building for Windows. Its feature flags turn on just the API areas used so far: `Win32_Foundation`, `Win32_System_SystemInformation` and `Win32_System_Threading`. Release builds are set to optimise for a small binary (`lto`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip`).
- **`rust-toolchain.toml`**: Pins stable Rust and installs the Windows target (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), `rustfmt` and `clippy`.
- **`.cargo/config.toml`**: Builds the C runtime into the `.exe` (`+crt-static`), so it runs on machines without the Visual C++ Redistributable.
- **`src/main.rs`**: A small example that calls `GetCurrentProcessId`, `GetSystemInfo` and `GetTickCount64` from an `unsafe` block with a `// SAFETY:` comment, returning `windows::core::Result`. Building for any other platform stops with a clear `compile_error!` message, though the compiler also prints a few follow-on errors after it.

**Things to know:**
- When you call a new part of the Windows API, add its feature flag to `Cargo.toml`, for example `Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging` for message boxes and windows. The [windows crate docs](https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/) show which flag each function needs.
- If you only need plain C-style function calls and want faster compiles, the lower-level `windows-sys` crate (v0.61) is an alternative.
- To check from a non-Windows machine, use `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. On Windows, `cargo build` and `cargo run` work normally.

Nothing is committed yet.
